content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity).**

**What I found.** The audit right binding us lives in Article II.IV(b) (p0073), with its cost-allocation sentence displaced up at p0064. There is no audit heading, so this matches the planner's suspicion that the right was buried in the volume-billing/record-keeping terms.

**Elements already at or above the playbook position:**
- Independent CPA or audit professional, selected by mutual agreement
- Scope limited to "appropriate accounting records" — no right of access to our systems
- 30-day lead time from Licensor's written request
- Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found (preferred threshold, not just the 10% fallback)

**Why it still fails the fallback:** no frequency cap whatsoever. Licensor could serve repeated audit requests, which is unlimited-audit / walk-away territory and misses the fallback's "once per year." The clause is also silent on business hours and on binding the third-party auditor to confidentiality — the confidentiality article covers the parties, not an outside CPA.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** a single proviso appended to p0073 capping audits at one per twelve months, requiring 30 days' prior written notice, confining them to normal business hours without unreasonable interference, and binding the auditor to confidentiality no less protective than the Agreement. I deliberately left the 5% cost-shift and the records-only scope untouched, since both already favor us — reopening them risks trading away a better-than-fallback bargain.

input.quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
input.rationale: Article III is a one-way ownership clause: Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and "Intellectual Property Rights" (1.6) is defined solely as rights "of Licensor". "Derivative Work" (1.3) sweeps in "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology", so the bespoke customization and unique client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in Licensor. There is no assignment to us and no licence back beyond the limited, non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence, which terminates on expiry with an obligation to return everything (Article XXI). The Agreement is also silent on our data: Confidential Information (1.2) protects only information disclosed to Licensee, and nothing confirms we retain our trading, order, client and account data. Vendor keeping its platform is fine, but the clause fails even the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables) and leaves Customer Data ownership unaddressed. We added a narrow carve-out: we retain our data and IP; paid-for deliverables are assigned to us with Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP and granting a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded materials; and no joint ownership is created.

proposal.summary: Add Licensee ownership of its data and of paid-for customization deliverables, with a licence-back of embedded Licensor IP and no joint ownership.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article III gives Licensor ownership of the Licensed Technology and all Derivative Works but says nothing about our data or about the customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), leaving us with no ownership and no surviving licence. We have added a carve-out confirming we retain our trading and client data, that paid-for deliverables are assigned to us subject to Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP (licensed back to us on a perpetual, royalty-free basis), and that no joint ownership is created; if Licensor prefers, we can instead take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense those deliverables.

input.quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
input.rationale:
Article III is a one-way ownership clause: Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and "Intellectual Property Rights" (1.6) is defined solely as rights "of Licensor". "Derivative Work" (1.3) sweeps in "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology", so the bespoke customization and unique client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in Licensor. There is no assignment to us and no licence back beyond the limited, non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence, which terminates on expiry with an obligation to return everything (Article XXI). The Agreement is also silent on our data: Confidential Information (1.2) protects only information disclosed to Licensee, and nothing confirms that we retain our trading, order, client and account data. Vendor keeping its platform is acceptable, but the clause fails even the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables) and leaves our data ownership unaddressed. We therefore added a narrow carve-out: we retain our data and IP; paid-for deliverables are assigned to us with Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP and granting a perpetual, royalty-free licence back for embedded materials; and no joint ownership is created.</parationale>

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

(i) "Monthly Notional Volume" means the US$ (US Dollar) equivalent of the primary currency traded Client turnover, provided that US$ (US Dollar) conversion should be made based upon the monthly revaluation rate (last business day) and volume should be rounded to the nearest million; and

(ii) For the avoidance of doubt, if any of the Monthly Notional Volume is reached in one relevant month, the fee rate per trade applicable to the highest Monthly Notional Volume band reached in that month shall apply to all trades (each way) in that month; not just to the trades within a particular band. For example, if in any given month the Monthly Notional volume traded is (US$10.1 billion), the fee rate per (US$1 million trade will be US$7 for the entire amount of US$10.1 billion.
III. Time of Payment
(a) Each payment for a particular calendar month shall be due no later than the (20th) day of the subsequent calendar month.

(b) The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly. In no event shall the amount payable by the Licensor be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded with the Licensed Technology multiplied by the applicable Fees set forth above.

(a) As a condition of Licensee receiving the grant of a license herein, Licensee agrees to maintain reasonable records relating to all trades conducted through the Licensed Technology and all other uses of the Licensed Technology by the Licensee under this Agreement. Licensee shall prepare and submit summary quarterly reports to Licensor no later than 20 days following the last business day of each calendar quarter, which reports must specify a complete record of usage of the Licensed Technology by the Licensee and shall accompany the payments made to Licensor.

(a) Simultaneously with the execution hereof, the Licensor shall issue to the Licensee 350,000 shares of its common stock as a bonus.

(b) Rebate Shares. During the period commencing on the Acceptance Date through the thirty six (36th) month anniversary of this Agreement, the Licensor shall remit to Licensee a series of rebates based upon the amount of Notional Volumes traded on the EPath FX Trading Platform by Licensee. The computation of the rebates received by Licensee shall be expressed as a fixed percentage (15%) of Billable Platform Fees paid by Licensee to Licensor. The rebates shall be payable in shares of Licensor's Common Stock; priced at $.25 cents per share. The amount of rebates earned by Licensee shall be calculated for each tranche of 30 Billion of Notional Volume traded in the EPath FX Platform by Licensee. The amount of shares earned by Licensee shall terminate at the earlier of, the expiration of the term of this Agreement or the receipt of Six (6,000,000) Million shares of Licensor's common stock by Licensee. By way of illustration, if the Licensee trades 30 Billion of Notional Volume on the Platform, with a Billable Platform Fee of $279,000. The rebate to Licensee will be calculated as follows: Rebate = 15% of $279,000 = $41,850; Shares of Licensor representing $41,850/$.25 = 167,400 shares of Licensor.

Kind: missing

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.

"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.

Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no express performance warranty anywhere. Article VII obliges Licensor only to use "commercially reasonable efforts to provide Error Corrections" (p0093) and to make Revisions available (p0094), which is a support covenant rather than a warranty, and Article VIX provides the Licensed Technology wholly "AS IS" with all warranties express and implied disclaimed, including any warranty that the technology is error-free, will meet Licensee's requirements, or that nonconformity to its Documentation can or will be corrected (p0110-p0116). That is the playbook's walk-away position: full "AS IS" with no conformance warranty and no remedy, so it fails even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund). Redline inserts the preferred express warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance to Documentation, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair/replace/refund remedy and carves it out of the disclaimer; the fallback 90-day period is offered in the comment.

When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.

Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

ops.text: (l) INSURANCE. Licensor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than US$1,000,000 per occurrence and US$2,000,000 in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than US$2,000,000; (iii) cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than US$5,000,000, covering Licensor's processing, storage or transmission of Licensee's data and Confidential Information; and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Licensor shall provide Licensee with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

The Licensee agrees to accept and use the Confidential Information only for the purpose of carrying out its authorized activities under this Agreement. In the event the Licensee is required to disclose the Confidential Information by an order of a court or governmental agency, then the Licensee shall first give written notice to Licensor to allow Licensor to make a reasonable effort to obtain a protective order or other confidential treatment for the Confidential Information.

(b) NON SOLICITATION. For purpose of this Article the term "Solicit" means any affirmative recruitment specifically aimed at one or more individuals identified by name, title or affiliation, but shall not mean generally advertising job openings or any activities that constitute follow-up to individuals who respond to job opening advertisements or who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries.

ARTICLE XX CERTAIN OTHER EVENTS OF TERMINATION (a) Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control. (i) a transaction or series of related transactions that results in the sale or other disposition of all or substantially all of Licensee's assets; or (ii) a merger or consolidation in which Licensee is not the surviving corporation or in which, if Licensee is the surviving corporation, the shareholders of Licensee immediately prior to the consummation of such merger or consolidation do not, immediately after consummation of such merger or consolidation, own stock or other securities of Licensee that possess a majority of the voting power of all Licensee's outstanding stock and other securities and the power to elect a majority of the members of Licensee's board of directors; or (iii) a transaction or series of related transactions (which may include without limitation a tender offer for Licensee's stock or the issuance, sale or exchange of stock of Licensee) if the shareholders of Licensee immediately prior to the initial such transaction do not, immediately after consummation of such transaction or any of such related transactions, own stock or other securities of Licensee that possess a majority of the voting power of all Licensee's outstanding stock and other securities and the power to elect a majority of the members of Licensee's board of directors.

(b) In the event Licensee winds up, dissolves or otherwise ceases doing business, Licensor shall be entitled to terminate this Agreement immediately upon written notice to Licensee.

ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.

ARTICLE XXII RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL During the term of this Agreement, the Licensor shall have the right (the "Right of First Refusal"), for a period (the "Exercise Period") expiring at 11:59 PM (Eastern Time) on the fifth (5th) business day after the giving of written notice by the Licensee that it has received a bonafide offer from a third party to (ii) purchase all or substantially all of the assets of Licensee; or (ii) to engage in a merger or consolidation in which Licensee is not the surviving corporation or in which, if Licensee is the surviving corporation, the owners of Licensee immediately prior to the consummation of such merger or consolidation do not, immediately after consummation of such merger or consolidation, own stock or other securities of Licensee that possess a majority of the voting power of all Licensee's outstanding stock and other securities and the power to elect a majority of the members of Licensee's board of directors.
In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise in full the Right of First Refusal before the expiration of the Exercise Period, the
Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding submitted: deviation (Rule IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What the document does:** Article III (p0048) vests all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology and "all Intellectual Property Rights therein" in Licensor, with "Intellectual Property Rights" (1.6) defined only as Licensor's rights and "Derivative Work" (1.3) capturing "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology."
- **Why it fails the fallback:** The bespoke customization / unique client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) (p0087) falls within Licensor's ownership with no assignment and no licence back — only the limited non-exclusive Field-of-Use licence, which terminates with the Agreement and triggers a return-of-materials obligation (Article XXI). There is also no Customer Data ownership provision anywhere; Confidential Information (1.2) protects only information disclosed *to* Licensee, so our trading, order, client and account data is unaddressed.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** a "Notwithstanding the foregoing" carve-out inserted after Article III confirming (i) we retain all rights in Licensee Data and our IP, (ii) paid-for deliverables are assigned to us with Licensor retaining its pre-existing IP and granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence for materials embedded in those deliverables, and (iii) no joint ownership is created. The comment offers the fallback (perpetual licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables) if Licensor resists assignment.
- Licensor's retention of the platform itself is not challenged.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration)**

The agreement gives us no warranty protection at all:

- **No express warranty exists.** Article VII contains only support covenants — "commercially reasonable efforts to provide Error Corrections" (p0093) and availability of Revisions (p0094) — not a conformance or workmanlike-performance warranty.
- **Article VIX is a full "AS IS" disclaimer** (p0110–p0116): all warranties express and implied disclaimed, with express negation of error-free operation, fitness for our requirements, and even that "NONCONFORMITY TO ITS DOCUMENTATION CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED."

That combination is the playbook's walk-away position, so it fails the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with repair, replace or refund) rather than merely falling short of preferred.

**Redline (validated ok:true):**
1. Inserted an express warranty after the Article VIX heading: workmanlike services, 12-month conformance of the Licensed Technology to Documentation and Specifications, no malicious code, compliance with applicable law, with a repair / replace / re-perform / refund remedy at Licensor's option.
2. Amended p0110 to open "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE, ..." so the disclaimer no longer swallows the new warranty.

The comment offers the fallback 90-day conformance period as a landing zone if Licensor pushes back on 12 months.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: (k) REPRESENTATION BY COUNSEL. Each party acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to be represented by separate independent counsel in the negotiation of this Agreement
input.rationale: No insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement: the only occurrence of "insurance" is p0051, which merely makes Licensee responsible for taxes, duties and insurance charges on payments, and the GENERAL PROVISIONS section (p0144-p0159) runs from Governing Law through Representation by Counsel with no insurance sub-clause. Licensor supplies and supports the E-Path FX platform and receives Licensee's data and Confidential Information, so the playbook expects standard vendor coverage; absence of any coverage for a vendor processing our data is walk-away territory. Inserted the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request) as a new sub-clause (l) after p0159, with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback flagged in the comment.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:

content.text:
**Finding: missing (INSURANCE)**

The Agreement has no insurance covenant. The single reference to "insurance" (p0051) is only a cost pass-through obliging *Licensee* to bear insurance charges — it imposes nothing on Licensor. GENERAL PROVISIONS (p0144–p0159) covers governing law through representation by counsel with no insurance sub-clause, and no separate insurance heading exists in the outline.

Because Licensor supplies and supports the E-Path FX trading platform and handles our data and Confidential Information, the complete absence of coverage sits in walk-away territory under the rule. I inserted a new sub-clause (l) after p0159 at the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request, term plus one year), with the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback offered in the negotiation comment. Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted.

input.quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
input.rationale: The fee architecture is purely usage-based and meets the preferred position: user fees are a tiered rate "per US$1million traded (for each one-way part of the trade)" applied to actual Monthly Notional Volume (p0056–p0058, p0070). A full-text review found no minimum purchase commitment, no committed volume, no take-or-pay, no shortfall or make-whole payment, and no volume cap on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shall be no less than" and "per month" return nothing of that character. The only fixed amounts are the already-advanced $35,000 initial payment (p0051) and $2,500 per month for Technical Support Services (p0086), which are fees for ordered services rather than a purchase commitment. The volume tiers operate only to reduce the per-million rate as volume rises, so higher volume benefits us. The "In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded ... as being traded" language in p0070 is a floor tied to actual recorded trades, not a committed minimum. Noted for context only (not a deviation under this rule): the initial term is 36 months and renewal is at Licensor's option (p0049) — term/renewal control is addressed under the term and termination rules, not as a take-or-pay exposure, since no spend is committed over that term. No redline proposed.

The volume tiers operate only to reduce the per-million rate as volume rises, so higher volume benefits us. The "In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded ... as being traded" language in p0070 is a floor tied to actual recorded trades, not a committed minimum. input.quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
input.rationale: The fee architecture is purely usage-based and meets the preferred position: user fees are a tiered rate "per US$1million traded (for each one-way part of the trade)" applied to actual Monthly Notional Volume (p0056–p0058, p0070). A full-text review found no minimum purchase commitment, no committed volume, no take-or-pay, no shortfall or make-whole payment, and no volume cap on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shall be no less than" and "per month" return nothing of that character. The only fixed amounts are the already-advanced $35,000 initial payment (p0051) and $2,500 per month for Technical Support Services (p0086), which are fees for ordered services rather than a purchase commitment. The volume tiers operate only to reduce the per-million rate as volume rises, so higher volume benefits us. The "In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded ... as being traded" language in p0070 is a floor tied to actual recorded trades, not a committed minimum. Noted for context only (not a deviation under this rule): the initial term is 36 months and renewal is at Licensor's option (p0049) — term/renewal control is addressed under the term and termination rules, not as a take-or-pay exposure, since no spend is committed over that term. No redline proposed.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no transition-assistance or data-return provision anywhere. Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138) is entirely one-directional: the licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information back to Licensor within five days with officer certification, while "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." Nothing obliges Licensor to help us migrate or to return our own data. Article X confidentiality (p0124) binds only Licensee and contains no return/destruction mechanic that could serve, and the only other termination articles (XIX insolvency p0132-33, XX change of control p0134-37, XXIII p0142) are silent. This matters because the Licensed Technology is a hosted platform through which we receive market data and enter trading tickets (p0033, p0021), so our order, trade and account records sit on Licensor's systems; on termination we would have no contractual right to recover them, which falls at or near the walk-away position (no data return). We therefore insert the preferred position at p0138 as a new subsection (c): up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; 90 days of assistance with the 30-day export is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance and Licensee data return/deletion obligation into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property; it gives us no exit path and no right to recover our own trade and account data held on the Licensed Technology. We have added a reciprocal provision giving up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; we can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback provided the 30-day data return stays.

ops.text: Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Licensee all Licensee data, trade, order and account records and other Licensee information in Licensor's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such data, records and information from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to Licensee.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no transition-assistance or data-return provision anywhere. Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138) is entirely one-directional: the licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information back to Licensor within five days with officer certification, while "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." Nothing obliges Licensor to help us migrate or to return our own data. Article X confidentiality (p0124) binds only Licensee and contains no return/destruction mechanic that could serve, and the only other termination articles (XIX insolvency p0132-33, XX change of control p0134-37, XXIII p0142) are silent. This matters because the Licensed Technology is a hosted platform through which we receive market data and enter trading tickets (p0033, p0021), so our order, trade and account records sit on Licensor's systems; on termination we would have no contractual right to recover them, which falls at or near the walk-away position (no data return). We therefore insert the preferred position at p0138 as a new subsection (c): up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; 90 days of assistance with the 30-day export is available as a fallback.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall payment, or volume cap on Licensee. Fees sit at the playbook's **preferred** position: usage-based only, calculated monthly on actual Monthly Notional Volume at a tiered per-US$1m rate (US$7.50 down to US$5.00), where the tiers only *lower* our rate as volume grows. The tiered pricing flagged in the planner hint is a volume discount in our favour, not a commitment.

The only fixed sums are the already-advanced US$35,000 initial payment and US$2,500/month for Technical Support Services — fees for ordered services, not committed purchases. The "in no event shall the amount payable be less than the amount recorded as being traded" sentence in the payment clause is a floor tied to actual recorded trades, not a minimum volume.

Noted for context but not flagged here: the 36-month initial term with renewal at Licensor's option. Because no spend is committed across that term, this creates no take-or-pay exposure and belongs to the term/termination rules rather than MINCOMMIT (avoiding a double flag on the same commercial term).

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no transition-assistance or data-return provision anywhere. Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138) is entirely one-directional: the licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensed Technology, documentation and Confidential Information back to Licensor within five days with officer certification, while "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination." Nothing obliges Licensor to help us migrate or to return our own data. Article X confidentiality (p0124) binds only Licensee and contains no return/destruction mechanic that could serve, and the only other termination articles (XIX insolvency p0132-33, XX change of control p0134-37, XXIII p0142) are silent. This matters because the Licensed Technology is a hosted platform through which we receive market data and enter trading tickets (p0033, p0021), so our order, trade and account records sit on Licensor's systems; on termination we would have no contractual right to recover them, which falls at or near the walk-away position (no data return). We therefore insert the preferred position at p0138 as a new subsection (c): up to six months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter; 90 days of assistance with the 30-day export is available as a fallback.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity)**

**What I found.** The Agreement has no transition-assistance or data-return provision anywhere:

- **Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138)** runs one way only — licenses terminate automatically, and *we* must ship all Licensed Technology, APIs, documentation and Confidential Information to Licensor within five days plus officer certification. It closes with "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination," with no reciprocal obligation on Licensor.
- **Article X confidentiality (p0124)** binds only the Licensee and contains no return/destruction mechanic that could partially serve.
- The other termination provisions — Article XIX insolvency (p0132–33), Article XX change of control (p0134–37), Article XXIII (p0142) — are silent on exit mechanics.

**Why it matters here.** The Licensed Technology is a hosted platform through which we receive consolidated market data and enter trading tickets (p0021, p0033), so our order, trade and account records reside on Licensor's systems. With no export right, termination would leave us unable to recover them — at or near the playbook's walk-away position.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** New subsection (c) inserted after p0138 at the preferred position: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty (30) days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter. The comment flags 90 days of assistance as an acceptable fallback provided the 30-day data return survives.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — E-Path FX Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of 18 rules assessed, **12 are open** (9 deviations, 3 missing clauses) and **6 are compliant**. The risk profile is heavily one-sided in the Licensor's favour.

Three issues are critical and, in our view, must be resolved before signature:

- **Indemnification** — Article XII is a one-way indemnity running only from us to Licensor, and Article XIII expressly excludes any Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims. There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the document.
- **IP and data ownership** — Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and, through the "Derivative Work" definition, the bespoke customization and client front end we commission and pay for under Article VII(b). The Agreement is silent on ownership of our trading, order, client and account data.
- **Limitation of liability** — the cap protects only Licensor and is set at one half of amounts paid, while our liability is uncapped and expanded by the Article XII indemnity. There are no carve-outs of any kind.

Compounding these, we have **no exit**: the term is 36 months, renewal is at Licensor's unilateral option for a further seven years, there is no termination for convenience, no performance warranty (the platform is supplied wholly "AS IS"), no transition assistance or data-return right, and no vendor insurance. Assignment is barred for us with no successor carve-out while Licensor may assign freely, and a Licensee change of control automatically terminates the Agreement absent consent.

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum volume commitment, no MFN and no liquidated damages** on us; pricing is genuinely usage-based; and governing law and venue (New York law, exclusive New York courts) match our preferred position.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Arts. XII–XIII) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. III; defs. 1.2, 1.3, 1.6) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions, § (c) Assignment; Arts. XX, XXII |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. VI; General Provisions § (c); Art. XX) |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Arts. IV, XIX–XXI, XXIII) |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Arts. IV, V, XXI, XXIII) |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (def. 1.5; Arts. II, X) |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. II.IV(b) (fee schedule / audit cost allocation) |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. X(b)) |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (Art. IV) |
| 13 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI, Effect of Termination) |
| 14 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX; Art. VII) |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (fee schedule; Art. XXII) |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions (fee schedule) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | General Provisions |

### Notes on the compliant items

- **Exclusivity / non-compete / minimum commitment / MFN:** nothing in the Agreement restricts our sourcing, volume or pricing behaviour. The licence is expressly non-exclusive and fees are a tiered per-US$1m rate on actual traded volume, with higher volume reducing the rate. No redlines proposed.
- **Liquidated damages:** no penalty, shortfall or early-termination fee is payable by us; Article XXIII bars termination damages for both parties. The audit cost-shift (triggered only above a 5% discrepancy) is a cost-reimbursement mechanic, not a penalty.
- **Governing law:** New York law with exclusive New York courts, no arbitration clause. Venue is framed as the City of New York rather than New York County — noted only, not redlined.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit at or near the playbook's walk-away positions and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a one-way Licensee indemnity** (Arts. XII–XIII). Article XIII also expressly excludes Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement, so any indemnity we insert must override it. Fallback available: customary infringement exclusions with a 3x annual fees super-cap.
2. **Licensor-only liability cap at one half of amounts paid, with our liability uncapped and no carve-outs** (Art. XIII). Fallback: mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
3. **Automatic termination on our change of control** (Art. XX), with consent deemed reasonably refused wherever Licensor believes its interests are affected — combined with a blanket bar on our assignment, no successor carve-out, unrestricted Licensor assignment, and a Licensor right of first refusal over our M&A (Art. XXII). Fallback: mutual assignment to successors on written notice.
4. **No Licensee termination for convenience** across a 36-month term. Fallback: 60–90 days' notice with fees capped at three months.
5. **Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option** (Art. IV), which we cannot decline and which is uncapped on price — and which conflicts with the mutual-written-agreement mechanic in Arts. IV.II and IV.III. Fallback: 60-day opt-out, uplift capped at 5%.
